new_statements.quote: The most prominent phonetic correlate of stress is pitch, as stressed syllables are articulated with a higher pitch than unstressed syllables. They also tend to be articulated at a higher volume. Word stress is generally predictable in Pokomchi', as it falls almost exclusively on the last syllable in a word, regardless of the syllable weight of this syllable [...] There are few exceptions to this, most of which are borrowings from Spanish [...] There are certain instances of original Pokomchi' words that do not follow predictable stress patterns, and these are so indicated in all phonemic and phonetic transcriptions. The most notable of these is the word /čaxari/ 'What?'.

new_statements.relation_note: Same placement as the catalog record (StressTyp2 rule 01/001/0001.. = fixed final). Adds detail: weight-insensitive, pitch as the correlate, loanword and one lexical exception. Describes Western Pokomchi' (San Cristóbal Verapaz area).
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the final syllable of the word, independent of syllable weight; the phonetic cue is higher pitch (and louder volume). Fn. 6 (p. 20) adds that vowel length and word stress are independent.
new_statements.exceptions: Spanish loans keep Spanish stress (e.g. [meša] 'table', [wakaš] 'cow', [šawela] 'Isabelle', [maŋka] 'mango', all with penultimate stress); the native word /čaxari/ 'What?' has non-final stress, explained as a fossilized hybrid of /čih xarik/ and /ča:x wo' xarik/; that word occurs in the San Cristóbal dialect only.
new_statements.identity_note: Weichel 2006 describes Western Pokomchi' (San Cristóbal Verapaz dialect area); the /čaxari/ exception is noted as San Cristóbal only. Mayers 1958 (unopened) is on Pocomchi generally.

tone.quote: El acento se refiere a la fuerza con que se pronuncia la sílaba de una palabra. En el idioma Poqomchi’ se utiliza el acento fijo y se da la elevación fónica en la última sílaba. Por lo que no necesita ser graficado o escrito por medio de una tilde, puesto que todas las palabras son agudas. El acento afecta de igual forma a las palabras, ya sean radicales, derivadas o compuestas.
tone.locator: ch. II §3.1 'El acento en el idioma Poqomchi'', p. 49 (page footer; TOC lists p. 50)
tone.translation: Stress refers to the force with which the syllable of a word is pronounced. The Poqomchi' language uses fixed stress, and the pitch elevation falls on the last syllable. It therefore does not need to be written with an accent mark, since all words are final-stressed. Stress affects words in the same way whether they are roots, derived or compound.
